name: What is the difference between using spackle and joint compound for wall patches?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between using spackle and joint compound for wall patches?

acceptedAnswer.text: While pre-mixed spackle works well for tiny nail holes, deeper holes and larger cutouts require true joint compound and structural tape to prevent future cracking. Spackle shrinks, dries brittle, and lacks the structural bonding strength needed to bridge gaps larger than an inch. Joint compound, especially setting-type mud used with fiberglass or paper tape, forms a durable, sandable bond across seams. For holes larger than a couple of inches, adding wood backing and real drywall core pieces is essential.
acceptedAnswer.description: Spackle is only suitable for tiny nail holes. Larger repairs require joint compound, drywall tape, and proper backing to prevent cracking and shrinking over time.
